name: Centro Historico (Plaza Mayor)
tagline: Colonial heart around the great square
description: The whitewashed historic core built around the vast cobbled Plaza Mayor, ringed by low-rise heritage houses, cafes, restaurants, and shops. It is the most walkable, atmospheric, and touristy part of town, buzzing on weekends and quieter midweek.
bestFor: Nomads wanting atmosphere, cafes, and everything walkable from their door
pros: Best choice of cafes and restaurants

name: Plaza del Carmen area
tagline: Quieter streets by the Carmen church
description: The calmer pocket around the Carmen church and its small plaza, just north of the main square. It keeps the colonial charm and easy walkability but with a gentler, more residential feel and slightly fewer crowds.
bestFor: Those wanting colonial charm and a calmer base near the centre

name: Vineyard and Pozos Azules outskirts
tagline: Rural edge toward vineyards and ponds
description: The semi-desert outskirts stretching toward the vineyards and the Pozos Azules ponds, dotted with fincas, guesthouses, and larger rentals. It offers space, big skies, and quiet, at the cost of needing transport into town.
bestFor: Nomads with transport wanting space, nature, and quiet away from crowds
cons: Need a car, bike, or taxi

name: Sachica road (fossil sites)
tagline: Open valley toward the fossil trail
description: The road running west toward Sachica and the fossil sites such as El Fosil and the Kronosaurus museum. This open valley area is spread out and rural, suiting longer stays in fincas with easy access to the region's palaeontology.
bestFor: Long-stay visitors keen on fossils, cycling, and wide-open landscapes
